title: Blade: Trinity
full_review:
Sitting through "Blade: Trinity" (New Line), the third -- and reportedly final -- installment in the Marvel Comics adapted vampire trilogy, is about as fun for viewers as a garlic bubble bath would be for the movie's fanged femme fatale.

Wesley Snipes returns as the titular slayer, a brooding half-mortal, half-vampire, who in this go-round must join forces with a team of vampire-hunters (Jessica Biel and Ryan Reynolds) to battle an army of bloodsuckers (led by Parker Posey) bent on resurrecting the granddaddy of all undead, Dracula (Dominic Purcell) -- here re-imagined as an ancient Sumerian demon -- to spawn a vampiric master race.

A haggard looking Kris Kristofferson is also back as Blade's mentor, Whistler.

Violent and vacuous, the bloodfest, written and directed by David S. Goyer, dishes out the same headache-inducing action sequences, tedious gore and cheesy dialogue as did the first two installments.

Hopefully, "Blade: Trinity" will drive a stake through any future films in this forgettable franchise.

Due to excessive violence, much profanity and rough language, the USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted.
